name: Builders and Healers Work First
description: Villagers practise their selected job on their own: about three times in four, each time the game chooses what a villager does, a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building first tries that job's own work, at any food level; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, the game chooses exactly as it always has. The one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. What the work is -- which crop, project, patient or study -- is the game's own choice, with its own technology levels and buildings, so nothing starts that the game itself would not allow. Researchers never take the place of a farming attempt, and Parenting is left to the game and the Birth Control patches. **This patch never sends a builder to start a project nobody was ever dropped on; it only puts builders first to carry on work that was started**. A builder with no building work to carry on does "Doing exercise" instead (Building practice), when the village has more than 250 food. Healers heal the sick, or study medicine once Medicine 2 has been researched. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp. Catch-up's low-food rule still wins: at 250 food or less a villager with Farming 20 or more farms, whatever their job. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the Origins-exclusive base appends does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.
behavior_changes: Whenever the adult scheduler (or the catch-up worker's pick dispatch, 0x45BFC0 returning to 0x45BFC5) asks the work dispatcher to start a job, for a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building (Farming 0, Parenting 1, Healing 2, Research 3, Building 4), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the caller sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the caller's own request runs unchanged. Parenting is never put first. Research never displaces a Farming request.

About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler and once per run of the catch-up worker (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the caller's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game.
Builders never start a project nobody was dropped on: The Secret City's Building case only continues projects above 0%, so a builder is always put first.

Exercise: when a builder's Building work started nothing (including when Building was the caller's own request, which the companion then dispatches itself on the roll), the food total [0x582490] is above 250 and the villager's current action (record+0xF24) did not change, the companion starts the game's own "Doing exercise" (do-action 0x455570, action 0x96), whose step raises Building through the standard practice roll.
At 250 food or less a healer's pick is also dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt, as Builders Fix Huts When Idle already does for builders.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: The Secret City's hook is the dispatcher stub that Builders Fix Huts When Idle places in the page Origins appends, which resolves this DLL's VvfpWorkFirstFirst itself; without this row the DLL is not shipped and the stub runs the stock code.

A villager with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose; the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and a villager with no selected job are untouched.
Parenting (job 1) is never put first, and the catch-up worker's Parenting pick (its 5% conception attempt) is not touched: births stay under the Birth Control patches.

What the work does -- which crop, project, hut, patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice, with its technology levels and buildings; the Farming cases start no tool or sack job (those stay drop-only) and no puzzle work.
In catch-up, the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x45BFAB: 250 food or less and Farming 20 or more) is not one of the calls the hook acts on, so Farming wins exactly as in the stock game.
Nothing is written to the save or any file.
